subject: science
cluster: The solar system and the universe

items.prompt:
What keeps the planets orbiting the Sun?
A) The Moon
B) The Sun's gravity
C) Wind
D) Magnetism only

steps: The Sun's gravity pulls the planets into orbit.

items.prompt:
What keeps moons in orbit around a planet?
A) The planet's gravity
B) The Sun's light
C) Air
D) Nothing

steps: A planet's gravity holds its moons in orbit.

items.prompt:
A huge collection of billions of stars held together by gravity is a:
A) Planet
B) Galaxy
C) Moon
D) Comet

steps: A galaxy is a vast, gravity-bound group of stars.

items.prompt:
Why does the Sun control the orbits of the planets?
A) It is the brightest
B) It has by far the most mass, so its gravity is strongest
C) It is the closest star
D) It is the smallest
items.answer: B) It has by far the most mass, so its gravity is strongest

steps: The Sun's huge mass gives it the strongest gravity.

items.prompt:
Without the Sun's gravity, a planet would:
A) Orbit faster
B) Move in a straight line off into space
C) Stop completely
D) Fall into the Sun
items.answer: B) Move in a straight line off into space

steps: With no inward pull, the planet would travel straight.

items.prompt:
What holds the stars of a galaxy together?
A) Gravity
B) Sunlight
C) Wind
D) Magnets only

steps: Gravity binds the stars in a galaxy.

items.prompt:
Objects with more mass have gravity that is:
A) Weaker
B) Stronger
C) Zero
D) Unrelated to mass

Why is an orbit described as a balance?
A) Gravity and motion cancel to zero
B) Gravity pulls the object inward while its motion would carry it straight, making a curved path
C) There is no gravity in orbit
D) The object is motionless
items.answer: B) Gravity pulls the object inward while its motion would carry it straight, making a curved path

steps: Gravity bends the object's straight-line motion into an orbit.
